I will not start from empty ground in my head. I will do it the way I have done for years, then move a little if I think it is worth the money. On 10.9 mu, I will keep most land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the steady way here and I have well water, so I can protect the yield when the weather turns dry. I will leave 8 mu for wheat-maize and 2.9 mu for cotton. I do not like cutting fertilizer too hard. If I save a few yuan on fertilizer and lose grain, that loss is bigger. So I will put enough base fertilizer, then topdress when the crop shows it needs feeding. For wheat, I will use better seed like most people around me, feed it a bit heavier, water about 3 times if the season is normal, and spray 2 times. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, plant soon after wheat comes off, give it enough nitrogen, water 2 times, and spray 2 times. Cotton is slower and needs more watching, so I will keep a smaller area, use improved seed, give it potash too, water about 3 times, and spray more times because insects can ruin it fast. I do what I have seen work on nearby fields: grain on the better part, cotton on the smaller piece, and I spend where losing yield would hurt me most.
